articles.title: Dragged, Shouted At, Thrown Into Van: CCTV Exposes Brutality on Elderly Women in Surat #breakingnews
articles.author: The Times Patriot
articles.excerpt: Surat: In a shocking incident from the Adajan area, an employee of a beggars’ shelter was removed from duty after CCTV footage showed her brutally mistreating two elderly women during an official rescue drive.

body.html:
Surat: In a shocking incident from the Adajan area, an employee of a beggars’ shelter was removed from duty after CCTV footage showed her brutally mistreating two elderly women during an official rescue drive.

The incident occurred on December 15 outside Shri Mahakaleshwar Mahadev Sainath Pavandham Shanidev Temple during an operation under the Bhikshuk Mukt Abhiyan. The Bhikshuk Gruh team, accompanied by Adajan police, had gone to rescue beggars as part of the administration’s drive to make the city beggar-free.

CCTV visuals that later went viral showed Divya Sonavane, a female employee of the beggars’ home, dragging a disabled elderly woman towards a police van, pushing her forcefully inside. She was also seen shouting at another elderly woman, pulling her clothes and dragging her along the road.

Following public outrage, the officer in charge of the beggars’ home, Jignesh Chaudhary, issued a 24-hour show-cause notice to Sonavane. As no satisfactory explanation was received and the violence was clearly evident in the footage, the administration ordered her immediate removal from duty.

The action has been cited as a strong message that inhumane conduct will not be tolerated in government-led welfare operations.

articles.title: Bengaluru Tragedy: Man Dies After Hospitals Turn Him Away, Passersby Ignore Wife’s Pleas
articles.author: The Times Patriot
articles.excerpt: Bengaluru: In a heart-wrenching incident highlighting alleged medical apathy and public indifference, a 34-year-old mechanic died after being forced to travel from hospital to hospital on a motorcycle while suffering from a heart attack in south Bengaluru.

body.html:
Bengaluru: In a heart-wrenching incident highlighting alleged medical apathy and public indifference, a 34-year-old mechanic died after being forced to travel from hospital to hospital on a motorcycle while suffering from a heart attack in south Bengaluru.

The deceased, Venkataramanan, a garage mechanic and resident of Balaji Nagar, developed severe chest pain around 3.30 am. Officials said he had suffered a minor heart attack earlier, and his condition deteriorated rapidly, leaving him extremely weak.

With no ambulance available, his wife placed him on a motorcycle and rode him to a nearby private hospital. The family alleges they were told that no doctor was available. They then went to another private hospital, where an ECG reportedly confirmed a mild heart attack. However, the hospital allegedly did not begin emergency treatment or arrange an ambulance, and instead advised them to take him to the Sri Jayadeva Institute of Cardiovascular Sciences in Jayanagar.

As the couple set off again on the motorcycle, they met with an accident on the way. CCTV footage shows Venkataramanan lying on the road in severe pain while his wife pleaded for help with folded hands. Despite her repeated requests, at least two cars, a tempo and a motorcycle passed by without stopping.

Several minutes later, a cab driver finally halted and helped rush Venkataramanan to a nearby hospital. Doctors there declared him dead on arrival.

Venkataramanan, who married in January 2020, is survived by his wife, a five-year-old son and an 18-month-old daughter. He was also the only surviving child of his mother, who had already lost her other five children earlier.

In a final act of compassion amid tragedy, the family donated Venkataramanan’s eyes, allowing his death to give sight to others.

articles.title: UP Horror: Man Kills Wife, Two Daughters, Buries Bodies Inside Home in Shamli
articles.author: The Times Patriot
articles.excerpt: Shamli (Uttar Pradesh): In a chilling case of domestic violence, a man has confessed to murdering his wife and two minor daughters and burying their bodies inside his house in Garhi Daulat village under Kandhla police station limits in Shamli district.

body.html:
Shamli (Uttar Pradesh): In a chilling case of domestic violence, a man has confessed to murdering his wife and two minor daughters and burying their bodies inside his house in Garhi Daulat village under Kandhla police station limits in Shamli district.

The accused, Farooq, admitted to killing his wife Tahira (32), elder daughter Afreen (12), and younger daughter Sareen (5) on the night of December 10, 2025. According to police, Farooq first shot Tahira while she was cooking in the kitchen. When Afreen woke up after hearing the noise, he shot her as well. He then strangled his younger daughter Sareen to death. His other three children remained asleep during the incident.

After committing the murders, Farooq dug a pit nearly nine feet deep inside the house and buried the bodies of all three victims to conceal the crime.

The crime came to light after Tahira and her two daughters were reported missing. Suspicion grew when they did not return for several days. On December 15, Farooq’s father, Daud, along with the village head, approached the police. During interrogation, Farooq initially tried to mislead investigators but later confessed to the crime.

Police said domestic disputes were the primary motive behind the murders. Farooq was reportedly enraged by frequent quarrels and objected to Tahira visiting her parental home without wearing a burqa, which further fueled tensions.

On receiving the confession, police reached the house in Garhi Daulat village and began excavation. Around 10 pm, the decomposed bodies of Tahira, Afreen and Sareen were exhumed. Superintendent of Police Narendra Pratap Singh confirmed that inquest proceedings were carried out and the bodies were sent for post-mortem examination.

SP Narendra Pratap Singh said the accused remains in custody and the investigation is ongoing. He added that the police will ensure the strictest possible legal action against the accused. The incident has sent shockwaves across the region.

articles.title: Son Kills Retired Railway Officer Parents, Dumps Bodies in River, Wanders Ghats After Crime
articles.author: The Times Patriot
articles.excerpt: Jaunpur/Varanasi (Uttar Pradesh): Police have cracked a sensational double murder case in which a man allegedly killed his parents with a grinding stone and dumped their bodies into the Gomti river.

body.html:
Jaunpur/Varanasi (Uttar Pradesh): Police have cracked a sensational double murder case in which a man allegedly killed his parents with a grinding stone and dumped their bodies into the Gomti river. The accused, identified as Ambesh Kumar, a resident of Ahmedpur village under Zafarabad police station limits, has been arrested and further investigation is underway.

According to police, Ambesh Kumar murdered his mother Babita Devi and father Shyam Bahadur on the night of December 8 following a heated argument over money. During interrogation, he confessed that he lost control and struck his mother on the head with a grinding stone, followed by a fatal attack on his father.

Police said that taking advantage of the house being empty, Ambesh stuffed both bodies into a sack, loaded it into his car, and drove around eight kilometres to Belav Ghat, where he dumped the sack into the Gomti river. To avoid suspicion, he returned home and pretended to search for his parents the next day, informing relatives and acquaintances about their alleged disappearance.

On December 12, Ambesh himself went missing. Concerned over the disappearance of her parents and brother, his sister Vandana, a resident of Katauna village under Sindhaura police station in Varanasi district, approached Zafarabad police and filed a missing persons complaint on December 9.

Taking the matter seriously, police formed three teams to investigate. During the probe, Ambesh was spotted in Varanasi, where he bathed in the Ganges and was seen wandering on the ghats. When he later returned towards his home, police apprehended him. During questioning, he broke down and confessed to the double murder.

Police said Shyam Bahadur was a loco pilot in the railways who had retired just four months ago. He was living with his family at his in-laws’ place and had three daughters, all married. Ambesh was their only son.

Further investigation revealed that Ambesh had married a woman from Kolkata five years ago during the COVID-19 pandemic. The marriage reportedly caused frequent disputes within the family. Police said Ambesh wanted to relocate to Kolkata with his wife and was allegedly demanding money from his parents, which led to repeated conflicts.

ASP City stated that an FIR has been registered under murder charges. Fifteen divers have been deployed to search for the bodies in the Gomti river. The accused is currently being interrogated, and efforts are ongoing to recover the bodies and collect further evidence.

Villagers said Ambesh had been living comfortably and had even purchased a car using his father’s money, which was allegedly used to dispose of the bodies. Following the revelation, anger and resentment have spread across the village.

articles.author: The Times Patriot
articles.excerpt: Hyderabad: A shocking and tragic incident was reported from Malkajgiri, where a mother allegedly threw her seven-year-old daughter from the top of a three-storey building, leading to the child’s death.

body.html:
Hyderabad: A shocking and tragic incident was reported from Malkajgiri, where a mother allegedly threw her seven-year-old daughter from the top of a three-storey building, leading to the child’s death.

According to police, the incident took place in Vasantapuri Colony under the Malkajgiri area. The accused, identified as Monalisa, lives there with her husband. Police said Monalisa has been suffering from mental illness for some time.

On Monday morning, Monalisa allegedly threw her daughter, Sharoni Mary, from the terrace of the three-storey building. The child sustained severe injuries in the fall. Local residents immediately rushed her to Gandhi Hospital for treatment.

Doctors at the hospital later declared the child brought dead. Following the incident, police registered a case and began an investigation. Further action will be taken based on the findings of the probe.

articles.title: Deadly Fog on Yamuna Expressway: 10 Vehicles Crash, Buses Catch Fire, 4 Killed in Mathura
articles.author: The Times Patriot
articles.excerpt: Mathura (Uttar Pradesh): Dense fog triggered a major multi-vehicle collision on the Yamuna Expressway near Milestone 127 in the Baldev area of Mathura around 4:30 am on December 16, 2025.

body.html:
Mathura (Uttar Pradesh): Dense fog triggered a major multi-vehicle collision on the Yamuna Expressway near Milestone 127 in the Baldev area of Mathura around 4:30 am on December 16, 2025. The accident involved seven buses and three cars, with several vehicles catching fire, leading to four deaths and injuries to 25 others.

According to officials, the chain collision began when three cars crashed due to near-zero visibility. Moments later, seven buses — including one Uttar Pradesh State Roadways bus and six private sleeper buses — rammed into them. The impact caused vehicles to burst into flames, creating panic among passengers who were asleep at the time.

Eyewitnesses said the fire spread rapidly, engulfing multiple vehicles and triggering chaos on the expressway. Eleven fire tenders were rushed to the spot, and emergency teams carried out swift rescue operations. The blaze was brought under control after sustained efforts.

Mathura Senior Superintendent of Police Shlok Kumar confirmed that poor visibility due to dense fog was the primary cause of the accident. He said four people — three bus passengers and one car occupant — died on the spot, while 25 injured persons were admitted to nearby hospitals. None of the injured are reported to be in critical condition.

Chief Minister Yogi Adityanath expressed grief over the incident and directed officials to ensure proper medical treatment for the injured. He announced an ex-gratia of ₹2 lakh each for the families of the deceased.

Authorities have advised motorists to exercise extreme caution while travelling on highways amid worsening winter fog conditions in Uttar Pradesh. The incident follows a similar fog-related pile-up on the Delhi–Mumbai Expressway in Nuh a day earlier, highlighting the increasing risks posed by low visibility during winter nights and early mornings.

articles.title: Ujjain Horror: Neighbour Kills 9-Year-Old Girl with 'Mogri', Police Expose Fall Story
articles.author: The Times Patriot
articles.excerpt: KHACHROD, MADHYA PRADESH: In a horrific crime that has shocked the Ujjain district, a nine-year-old girl was brutally murdered by a neighbour following a failed attempt to r@e her. The accused, identified as Riyaz Khan, has been arrested.

body.html:
KHACHROD, MADHYA PRADESH: In a horrific crime that has shocked the Ujjain district, a nine-year-old girl was brutally murdered by a neighbour following a failed attempt to r@e her. The accused, identified as Riyaz Khan, has been arrested.

The victim had visited her grandmother's house in Khachrod with her two sisters on Sunday. While playing outside, she went missing. Around 5:45 PM, neighbour Riyaz Khan brought the unconscious girl out of his house, claiming she had "fallen from above." The child had severe injuries to her head, face, and eyes and was rushed to a hospital in Ratlam, where she died during treatment on Monday.

Police investigation, however, quickly exposed the lie. Khachrod SDOP Akanksha Bichhote stated that medical examination showed no signs of a fall. Under strict interrogation, Khan confessed to the crime.

He revealed that he found the girl alone and attempted to molest her. When she screamed, he pushed her, rendering her unconscious. Fearing exposure, he then stuffed her into a sack and beat her with a mogri (a wooden washing paddle). Believing her to be dead, he later pretended to find her and presented the injured child to her grandmother.

The police have arrested Riyaz Khan, and a case has been registered.

articles.title: Days Before Wedding, Young Lawyer Found Dead in Gwalior; Family Alleges Betrayal by Fiancée
articles.author: The Times Patriot
articles.excerpt: Gwalior (Madhya Pradesh): A young lawyer died in Gwalior on Monday, just days before his scheduled wedding on December 30. The family has alleged that he took the extreme step after suffering emotional distress upon allegedly seeing his fiancée with another constable.

body.html:
Gwalior (Madhya Pradesh): A young lawyer died in Gwalior on Monday, just days before his scheduled wedding on December 30. The family has alleged that he took the extreme step after suffering emotional distress upon allegedly seeing his fiancée with another constable. Police have sent the body for post-mortem and said all aspects of the case are under investigation.

The deceased has been identified as Mrityunjay Chauhan, who lived in a rented house in Adarsh Puram area of Gwalior. He was practising law and was also pursuing a PhD. On Monday, he was found nging inside his room. Police reached the spot after receiving information and took the body into custody.

According to family members, Mrityunjay had been in a relationship with a female sub-inspector posted in Morena for the past five years, and their marriage was fixed for December 30. His mother said he went to meet his fiancée a day earlier than planned, where he allegedly saw her in her room with another constable. An argument reportedly followed, which escalated into a physical scuffle.

The family claimed that after the incident, Mrityunjay lodged a complaint at a police station regarding the assault, but no action was taken. He later called his mother, crying, and informed her about the incident. After this, he reportedly slipped into depression.

Before ending his life, Mrityunjay posted a status on social media quoting a dialogue from the recently released film ‘Tere Ishq Mein’, starring Dhanush and Kriti Sanon: “There is death in love, but no liberation.” His fiancée reportedly commented “bless” on the post.

Mrityunjay’s mother, Shivkumari, a government school teacher posted near Vijaypur, had travelled to Gwalior on Monday to meet her son. Instead, she received the news of his death. His father lives in Vadodara, Gujarat, while his elder brother lives separately. The parents have been living apart for several years.

After the body was taken down, police handed over Mrityunjay’s bracelet, chain and amulet to his mother. She broke down and said her son was her only support. She added that he had recently arranged her surgery in Delhi and used to call her daily to enquire about her health.

The mother further alleged that Mrityunjay had purchased two plots in Gwalior in the name of his girlfriend using his own share of money, and that there had been no earlier suspicion regarding the relationship.

Police said Mrityunjay lived alone with his dog. A thin plastic rope was used in the suicide. Food was found cooking in the kitchen, with some already eaten. An open liquor bottle and a glass were also found in the room. A thick rope was recovered as well, raising suspicion of prior planning.

Police officials said the case is being investigated from all angles. Further action will be taken after receiving the post-mortem report, call details and other evidence.

articles.title: Sweet Turned Deadly: Man Poisons Wife with Honey Over Affair Suspicion in Chandauli
articles.author: The Times Patriot
articles.excerpt: Chandauli (Uttar Pradesh): A 26-year-old woman died after being poisoned by her husband over suspicion of an illicit relationship in the Alinagar police station area of Chandauli district.

body.html:
Chandauli (Uttar Pradesh): A 26-year-old woman died after being poisoned by her husband over suspicion of an illicit relationship in the Alinagar police station area of Chandauli district. The accused husband, who is a drug addict, also consumed the poison and is currently undergoing treatment.

The incident occurred in Basni village, where Rohit Kumar lived with his wife Monica. According to police and villagers, Rohit had long suspected Monica’s character and frequently quarrelled with her. He was addicted to alcohol and other drugs, which often led to daily disputes between the couple. Tensions had reportedly escalated over the past two to three days.

Late on Sunday night (14 Dec 2025), Rohit returned home drunk, carrying sulphas tablets and honey. After having dinner together, he told his wife that he had brought honey and suggested having something sweet after the meal. Unaware of the danger, Monica agreed. Rohit had already mixed sulphas tablets into the honey. He fed a larger quantity to Monica and then consumed a small amount himself.

Soon after, both began to feel unwell. Hearing groaning noises from the house, nearby residents grew suspicious and informed the police. The Alinagar police rushed to the spot and shifted both to Pandit Kamalapati Tripathi District Hospital in a 108 ambulance.

Monica died during treatment at the hospital. As Rohit’s condition worsened, doctors referred him to the trauma centre, where he is currently admitted.

Dr Chandramani Singh, posted in the emergency ward, said the woman’s condition was extremely critical and she succumbed during treatment. Police have sent Monica’s body for postmortem, stating that the exact cause of death will be confirmed after the report.

Alinagar police station in-charge Anil Pandey said the case is being investigated from all angles. Further action will be taken based on the postmortem report and the complaint. Villagers alleged that Rohit’s drug addiction and constant suspicion of his wife were the main reasons behind the incident.

articles.excerpt: Agra (UP): A major uproar was witnessed in Mauhar village under the Kirawali police station area of Agra after local women vandalised a composite liquor shop located within the village limits on the Agra–Jaipur Highway.

body.html:
Agra (UP): A major uproar was witnessed in Mauhar village under the Kirawali police station area of Agra after local women vandalised a composite liquor shop located within the village limits on the Agra–Jaipur Highway.

The women alleged that their husbands had become habitual drinkers and were refusing to go to work, making it difficult to run their households. Angered by the situation, the women united and damaged the liquor shop, raising slogans and creating a commotion in the area. They stated that they would no longer tolerate the impact of alcohol on their families.

On receiving information, police reached the spot and questioned the women involved. Further investigation into the incident is underway.

The incident took place in Mauhar village, Kirawali police station area of Agra.
